legend: Ultrasonography shows a markedly cystic dilated duct containing a large intraductal papilloma; colour Doppler indicates the vascular flow.
A large multinodular papillary structure projects into the lumen of a large cyst (blue colour from localization dye).
A Low-power view shows an intraductal papilloma. B At higher power. Epithelial nests may be entrapped in biopsy site granulation tissue beyond the periphery and can mimic invasion.

diagnosis: Intraductal papilloma with ductal carcinoma in situ
legend: Low power shows a dilated duct containing papillary fronds (right) lined by non-atypical apocrine and columnar epithelium. The cribriform proliferation in the left portion of the lesion measures > 3 mm.

diagnosis: Intraductal papilloma with ductal carcinoma in situ
legend: Medium power shows monotonous epithelial cells with low-grade nuclei in the left portion of the papillary lesion. On the basis of cytology, architecture, and size (> 3 mm), this lesion is diagnosed as intraductal papilloma with ductal carcinoma in situ.

diagnosis: Intraductal papilloma with ductal carcinoma in situ
legend: ER staining shows strong diffuse positivity in ductal carcinoma in situ (left) but is patchy in the benign portion of the papilloma (right).

diagnosis: Intraductal papilloma with ductal carcinoma in situ
legend: CK5 is negative in ductal carcinoma in situ (left) and highlights the myoepithelial cells lining the fibrovascular cores in both portions of the papilloma. The benign epithelium is also negative for CK5 in this case, as the epithelium is apocrine and columnar. CK5 is typically positive in usual ductal hyperplasia lining papillomas.
Ultrasonography shows a markedly cystic dilated duct containing a large intraductal papilloma.
p63 immunostaining demonstrates myoepithelial nuclei lining fibrovascular stalks.
Cytoplasmic SMMHC staining demonstrates a continuous layer of myoepithelium.

diagnosis: Intraductal papilloma with usual ductal hyperplasia and myoepithelial hyperplasia
legend: The epithelial cells have crowded overlapping nuclei and are haphazardly arranged around slit-like spaces in the centre. The prominent spindle cells in the upper right are myoepithelium.

diagnosis: Intraductal papilloma with usual ductal hyperplasia and myoepithelial hyperplasia
legend: p63 staining highlights the myoepithelial cells in the upper right, in addition to myoepithelial nuclei lining the fibrovascular cores. Myoepithelial cells line the edge of the involved duct at the left.

diagnosis: Intraductal papilloma with usual ductal hyperplasia and myoepithelial hyperplasia
legend: CK14 staining is positive in usual ductal hyperplasia at the centre, which would have a mosaic ER staining pattern (not shown). CK14 also highlights the myoepithelial cells in the upper right.
Histology shows papillae with fibrovascular stalks lined by columnar and apocrine epithelium with myoepithelium.

A large papilloma fills a cystic space. The myoepithelial layer is evident in most of the papillae. The epithelial component ranges from a single layer of cuboidal to columnar cells to foci of usual ductal hyperplasia.
Large intraductalpapilloma with foci of usual ductalhyperplasia

A continuous layer of CK5/6-positive myoepithelium is present along the papillae of this large papilloma. Few foci of usual ductal hyperplasia (UDH) are present, and demonstrate the characteristic "checker board" pattern of immunoreactivity for CK5/6.
Intraductal papilloma with usual ductal hyperplasia, surrounding fibrosis and a core biopsy tract. Epithelial displacement is noted.
